title-proc.eng: Provision of services to support economic modelling of climate change and energy policies: Modelling of non-CO2 greenhouse gases, air pollutants, and LULUCF offsets

description-proc.eng: The European Green Deal is the roadmap for making the EU’s economy sustainable. It is a set of policy initiatives with the overarching aim of making Europe climate neutral by 2050. The "Economics of Climate Change, Energy and Transport" Unit (JRC.C.6) of the Joint Research Centre supports the European Commission’s European Green Deal by performing economics-based research in several areas related to energy and climate change. This work includes the development of a reference toolset of economic models and the completion of associated research activities to improve the models' reliability and robustness. The JRC.C.6 Unit is based in Seville, Spain. JRC.C.6 is seeking to strengthen its socio-economic research and modelling capabilities by expanding its coverage of modelling areas and by updating and improving its existing models and toolsets. The unit JRC.C.6 maintains, develops and applies a number of quantitative tools to analyse the impact of different policies on the energy demand and supply sectors, as well as tools for macro-economic modelling. This toolset comprises the EU and global partial equilibrium models POTEnCIA and POLES including their corresponding databases (notably JRC-IDEES), and the global general equilibrium model JRC-GEM-E3. All these tools are able to provide model output in terms of CO2 emissions. The comprehensive modelling of climate change mitigation scenarios requires additional information as regards non-CO2 greenhouse gas emissions as well as on emissions and sinks related to land use, land use change and forestry offsets (LULUCF). Besides, climate action can have important co[1]benefits in terms of reduced emissions of air pollutants and of improved air quality. This Framework Contract aims at supporting the operation of the abovementioned set of models by providing the JRC with data, methods and results relevant for the analysis of non-CO2 greenhouse gas emissions, emissions of air pollutants (including air quality impacts), and LULUCF offsets.

title-proc.eng: Public-private partnership for the design, financing, construction, reconstruction, rehabilitation and maintenance of local road infrastructure with payment by the public partner (availability-based) in the territory of the City of Sremska Mitrovica

description-proc.eng: The subject of the proposed project is the design, financing, construction, reconstruction, and rehabilitation of parts of the local road infrastructure of public importance, along with the provision of maintenance services for the local road infrastructure with public payment, on the territory of the City of Sremska Mitrovica, through the conclusion of a public-private partnership agreement between the City of Sremska Mitrovica and the private partner. Road infrastructure represents the backbone of the development and functioning of all possible human, economic, and other flows. Road infrastructure is an imperative of the social and economic standard both at the micro and macro level of a given locality, which essentially means the standard of living. A certain socio-political community measures its value primarily by the coverage of its road network – by its infrastructure facilities. The development of road infrastructure improves accessibility, which leads to the acceleration of regional development. With such an approach to the impact of investments, the overall benefits to society could outweigh the costs of investing in the development of road infrastructure. It is considered that the transport system is sustainable in the long term if it is able to provide the necessary capacity and level of service, if it is compatible with the locations it serves, if it is economical, relying on propulsion technology based on renewable and portable energy sources, if it is clean in order to maintain and regenerate the quality of the environment, and if it is cost-effective, and thus available to present and future generations. When it comes to public-private partnership, the basic elements of the concept of this model are clear allocation of responsibilities, risk sharing, and the duration of the partnership. Risk sharing enables each partner to assume the risk they can manage in the most adequate way, thereby achieving greater efficiency of such projects. The main goal of the development of road transport and road infrastructure is the establishment and development of a transport system that enables sustainable mobility of the population and provides support for the accelerated development of society and the economy, as well as strengthening competitiveness. Analyzing the current state of road infrastructure and the financial situation, it is evident that the City of Sremska Mitrovica does not have the possibility to independently invest in the construction of the planned sections, which is one of the essential prerequisites for the successful maintenance of road infrastructure while meeting the population’s needs for mobility. This project proposal is based on the idea of ensuring the availability of a portion of high-quality transport and accompanying infrastructure in urban zones and settlements through capital investment by the private partner. In addition to construction, reconstruction, and rehabilitation, the private partner will also prepare the project documentation, provide long-term regular maintenance across the entire territory and settlements, ensure protection and guarantee the quality of the works performed and services provided. The local self-government will not incur credit debt on this basis, given the way public-private partnership and concessions are regulated, while at the same time achieving the objectives of reducing budget expenditures, increasing the efficiency of public service delivery, and securing certain benefits for society as a whole. The compensation that the public authority will pay refers to the availability payment and infrastructure maintenance fee, and primarily relates to the payment for the service provided. With the received compensation during the contracted period, the private partner is obliged to finance and bear the financing costs for all obligations arising for it within this project, which primarily refers to: preparation of project documentation for the execution of works and maintenance of the subject infrastructure during the contracted period, capital investment (upgrading, construction, reconstruction, etc.), financing of investments and other costs arising within the project, maintenance and ensuring the availability of the subject road sections, and guaranteeing quality and maintaining the designed level of quality. In this way, by allocating risk to the private partner, optimizing procedures and phases, and assuming long-term responsibility for quality, the private partner will significantly better ensure quality than under the classical model based on construction and subsequent maintenance under a separate contract, which increases the risk of unclear boundaries of responsibility. Also, the classical method provides less guarantee for the quality of works, because the infrastructure is maintained independently, reducing the interest of both the contractor and the maintainer in delivering high quality. Under the proposed project, responsibility for all activities during the contracted period lies exclusively with the private partner. Of particular importance is the fact that the period in which the private partner would guarantee availability, quality, and maintenance — i.e., the period when the private partner is entitled to compensation — begins only once the infrastructure, or part of the infrastructure, has been fully completed in accordance with the implementation plan and execution timeline, and a proper handover certificate for the quality works performed has been issued.

title-proc.eng: Vessel Traffic System Upgrade Contract for Dublin Port Company

description-proc.eng: The Contracting Entity proposes to engage in a competitive process for the establishment of a contract for the Provision of Vessel Traffic Services (VTS) including Software, associated hardware, professional services, delivery, maintenance, and support. This procurement relates to the supply of a Vessel Traffic Services (VTS) system (software and any necessary supporting hardware, e.g. Radar, AIS, VHF Radio, Environmental Sensors, Device Communications, Network connectivity, Server based infrastructure). The service should include full project life cycle [Design, Build, Test, Parallel operation, Stability] also considering post-delivery support and maintenance. The aim of this project is to replace the current VTS ecosystem and supporting infrastructure where required (software and hardware), with the latest technologies providing for real time data and enterprise-wide integration. The aim is to replace the current VTS system infrastructure [Atlas VTS 9760]. At the very least the successful bidder will be required to integrate its solution to the current shipping system – PMIS – Port Control from Tidalis, to deliver the necessary functional requirements. It is anticipated this should be a standard integration. The system should also provide for remote access and mobile device capability. The new VTS solution DPC is seeking to acquire and implement includes the following high-level requirements: • Compliance with IALA standards, including S-1040, R0128 (V-128), and the G1111 series of guidelines, ensuring both operational and technical performance are aligned with global best practices. • Delivery of a robust and future-proofed VTS software ecosystem that: • Accepts, fuses, and displays data from radar, AIS, VHF, Electro-Optical (EO) sensors, and MetOcean systems. • Supports decision support tools (DST) for alarm handling, route monitoring, and incident response. • Provides record and replay functionality for traffic, sensor, and operator activity to support training and incident review. • Provision of a modern, ergonomic control room layout with at least two operator workstations and remote backup capabilities, aligned with BS EN ISO 11064 and IALA G1105/G1171 ergonomic design standards. • Deployment of an integrated sensor network delivering enhanced detection, redundancy, and target tracking across Dublin Port’s SHA and approaches. • Support for advanced AIS functionality including AIS AtoNs and message handling per G1111-4, with infrastructure coverage that ensures full vessel visibility across all navigational zones. • Provision of VHF radio systems meeting G1111-2 guidance, offering primary and backup coverage and seamless integration with operator terminals. • Compatibility with Electro-Optical and thermal imaging systems, particularly for situational awareness in berthing areas and areas of high risk. • A solution architecture that ensures resilience, minimal single points of failure, and high system availability, incorporating redundant power, communications paths, and server infrastructure. • Secure IT infrastructure design, with layered cybersecurity, compliance with GDPR and data retention policies, and robust access control mechanisms. • Open architecture to enable integration with existing and future port systems, including PMIS (Tidalis), berth monitoring tools, and third-party applications via secure APIs. • Scalable support for web-based and mobile access for authorised users, enabling situational awareness beyond the control centre in line with emerging operational demands. Delivery of post-implementation services including user training, system documentation, warranty, and long-term maintenance and support options. Must provide a solution where all VTS, radar and VHF Radio activity are recorded and stored for replay in incident management and operator training.

description-proc.eng: HEDI’s Defence Future Insights (DFI) provides strategic intelligence on emerging defence technologies by monitoring global R&T trends, weak signals, patent activity, and dual-use innovations. It supports capability-driven prioritisation and long-term defence planning by translating technological insights into defence applications. DFI also assesses innovation ecosystems, identifying key players, readiness levels, and adoption barriers, thus guiding targeted support and informed decision-making for EU defence stakeholders. In parallel, HEDI’s Defence Innovation Course aims to build a shared understanding of defence innovation across EU Ministries of Defence. It delivers practical training for mid-level officers and innovation managers to initiate and manage innovation effectively, addressing capability gaps identified through European Defence Innovation Network (EDIN) and stakeholder consultations. This cluster initiative encompasses four distinct projects, each tackling specific aspects of innovation management: LOT 1: Technology Watch and Landscaping: Provision of a regular and structured AI supported assessment of worldwide technological developments across both defence and non-defence sectors, identifying emerging trends, weak signals, and dual-use innovations that could impact EU security and defence; LOT 2: Military Utility Assessment: Focuses on evaluating the potential military applications of emerging technologies, assessing their operational utility, and identifying pathways for adoption into defence capability development; LOT 3: Consultancy services for needs assessment, market research, and market consultations: Provision of expert consultancy support for conducting market research and facilitating structured market consultations to bridge gaps between innovation suppliers and defence users; LOT 4: Defence Innovation Training Courses: Development and delivery of a structured, high-quality Defence Innovation Course. The first specific contract will focus on an Intermediate Level while potential follow-up contracts will address Basic and Advanced levels. The course is aimed at fostering a harmonized understanding of defence innovation across EU Member States while equipping participants with practical skills for managing and implementing innovation projects within innovation ecosystems. .

title-proc.eng: Purchase of Proteograph reagents ans SP100 Automation Instrument with XT

description-proc.eng: Turku Bioscience Centre intends to purchase Seer Proteograph reagents for deep discovery proteomics from 160 samples. Seer's special expertise is in nanoparticles, which are used to enrich proteins. The surface structure of the nanoparticles allows for protein enrichment without prior knowledge of the proteins to be enriched, making them suitable for a wide range of samples. In comparative studies, Seer's method has proven to be reproducible and unique in terms of performance. Seer's reagents are not available from others, and its closest competitors are not suitable for e.g. cell lysate samples. These combined unique properties are related to the particles: • Enrichment of low-abundance and previously undetected proteins. • Compatibility and demonstrated increase in the number of identified proteins from a wide range of samples including serum, plasma, cell culture media, and cell lysates. • Compatibility with samples from different species These properties distinguish Seer's method from affinity proteomics solutions of other possible provider´s reagents, making it the only suitable solution for research in question: • Compatibility with non-human samples • Seer’s method can be integrated into existing mass spectrometry-based workflows in Turku Bioscience Centre • Turku Bioscience Centre´s previous research was performed also with Seer reagents and to ensure comparability, the reagents must be from the same source. Seer Proteograph reagents are proprietary and compatible with Seer Proteograph system, which is the only solution in the market that meets all the necessary technical requirements to fulfil the uncompromising needs of the acquiring department as previously described. Reagents are planned to be used together with Seer SP100 Automation Instrument. Seer reagents require a special Seer instrument, SP100 Automation Instrument with XT, the only compatible with previously listed reagents. The instrument has the locked software, which was developed by SEER. The robot itself is manufactured by Hamilton, but ready-made control software for performing the SEER Proteograph protocol is not available anywhere else. The method is complex, and among other things, utilizes barcoded information on reagent tubes and containers, so its implementation with some generic laboratory automation is not practically possible.
